records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — A worker failure between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a permanent throttle key that silently prevents normal retrieval of that URL.
records.rationale: The diff shows in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-30 that SETNX and EXPIRE are called separately. This is a real race condition bug in the newly added code.

records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — A process failure between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves the retrieval throttle key without a TTL, permanently suppressing future imports for that URL.
records.rationale: The diff shows in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-30 that Redis SETNX and EXPIRE are called as separate operations. If the process crashes or fails between SETNX succeeding and EXPIRE being called, the key will exist without a TTL, permanently blocking future retrievals for that embed_url. This is a real race condition bug - the atomic SET with EX option should be used instead.

records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Remote article fetching has no open/read timeout, so an unresponsive embed host can indefinitely occupy a retrieval worker.
records.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, the code uses `open(url).read` without specifying any timeout options. This is called from `import_remote` method which fetches remote articles. The Ruby `open-uri` library by default has no timeout, meaning an unresponsive remote host could cause the worker to hang indefinitely. This is a real defect that could cause resource exhaustion in production.

records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Feed downloading and parsing have no timeout, allowing one stalled configured feed to hold a scheduled job worker indefinitely.
records.rationale: The diff shows poll_feed.rb at line 29 using `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without any timeout configuration. The `open-uri` library's `open` method by default has no timeout, meaning if the feed server is slow or unresponsive, the scheduled job worker will block indefinitely. This is a real defect in the new code - a stalled feed could hold up the Sidekiq worker.
